attribute.definition: Molecular weight of the compound in Daltons (g/mol), computed from structure by the curated descriptor route rather than a trained prediction; lower values are preferred because size above roughly 500 Da approaches the upper limit compatible with efficient passive intestinal diffusion and increases efflux-transporter recognition.
attribute.name: Molecular weight (Da)

bound_support.applicability_rationale: The passage reports that clinically relevant kinase inhibitors typically fall within approximately 380-500 Da and calls 500 Da close to the upper limit compatible with efficient passive diffusion; the candidate library consists of kinase inhibitors being screened for oral suitability, so the same upper edge applies.

interpretation.measurement: A reported typical range of approximately 380-500 Da for clinically relevant kinase inhibitors, with 500 Da described as close to the upper limit compatible with efficient passive diffusion.
interpretation.population_rationale: The candidates are kinase inhibitors intended for oral administration, the same population the reported range describes, so treating the 500 Da edge as the preference line is a defensible transfer of the heuristic.

rule.expected_change: Ranks compounds with lower computed molecular weight higher, placing compounds above the 500 g/mol heuristic below those at or under it, so that candidates whose size is compatible with efficient passive oral absorption come first.
rule.falsification_test: If molecular weight above 500 g/mol does not associate with reduced passive absorption or poorer oral exposure among kinase inhibitors in a reference set, the 500 g/mol bound and the ranking preference are falsified.

attribute.definition: Reported absolute or relative oral bioavailability (F%) in humans, as a measured pharmacokinetic parameter. Higher values indicate greater fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation intact. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: low F% compounds may still be clinically effective if the dose can be escalated.
attribute.name: Oral bioavailability (human, measured F%)
attribute.rationale: Directly measures the fraction of an oral dose reaching systemic circulation in humans. The objective requires oral administration; a measured human F% is a decision-relevant absorption parameter. Multiple claims report human F% values (e.g., 58%, 38-49%, 85-90%, 21.4%, 4.7%, 69-83%, 25%). No claim states a required minimum F%, so the rule ranks by value without a cutoff. The ordering is a preference, not a requirement: low F% compounds may still be clinically effective if the dose can be escalated.

rule.expected_change: Ranks candidates with higher measured human oral bioavailability above those with lower values.
rule.falsification_test: If a candidate with low measured F% is approved and clinically effective as an oral agent for the required targets, the preference ordering is challenged.

attribute.definition: Median of reported times to maximum plasma concentration after oral administration, in hours; when a source reports only a range, the range midpoint is used. Lower values indicate faster absorption. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: longer Tmax may still be compatible with oral bioavailability and efficacy.
attribute.name: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax, median of reported values)
attribute.rationale: Tmax is a direct measure of oral absorption rate. Cited claims report measured Tmax values of 4 h and 3 h and ranges of 1-4 h, 2-4 h, 3-4 h and 6-12 h for orally administered agents, establishing the quantity as measurable and decision-relevant, but no claim states a required Tmax, so the rule ranks by value without a cutoff. The ordering is a preference, not a requirement: longer Tmax may still be compatible with oral bioavailability and efficacy.

rule.expected_change: Ranks candidates with shorter Tmax above those with longer Tmax, without a numeric cutoff.
rule.falsification_test: If a candidate with longer Tmax is orally bioavailable and clinically effective, the ordering is not informative.
